Devon: seeing a sharp uptick in 5xx + gRPC stream resets in ded-cluster-usw2 around 09:17 UTC, coincides with nightly model warmup bursts. Latency spikes and connection resets mostly east-west. anyone else? :thinking:

oncall-bot: ALERT: net-telemetry anomaly detected for toprack-12 (tx_errors up) at 2026-02-12T09:17:28Z

Maria: can you dump the switch counters and a couple of host-side netstats from an affected pod? particularly interested in 'show interfaces counters', 'ethtool -S', and kernel dmesg for MSS/MTU warnings. @Chris?

Devon: pasted outputs — shortened for thread:

```
# show interfaces toprack-12 counters
port 1: rx_packets 1248912 tx_packets 1248720 rx_errors 0 tx_errors 1023 rx_drops 14 tx_drops 998
port 2: rx_packets 984123 tx_packets 984500 rx_errors 0 tx_errors 0 rx_drops 0 tx_drops 0
... (only port1 abnormal)
```

```
# ethtool -S eth0 on gpu-node-07
rx_packets: 523412
tx_packets: 523400
rx_missed: 2
tx_errors: 1100
hw_drops: 990
```

```
[  09.17.19] kernel: device eth0: Possible MTU mismatch: ICMP frag needed but DF set
[  09.17.23] kernel: tcp: severe reset: skb->len > MSS
```

Chris: looked at switch syslogs + ASIC counters. Found repeated ECMP 5-tuple hash flips when flows from same pod microburst across fanout links. Hash seeding on that ASIC seems to be rotating during control-plane flaps, causing path asymmetry. When path flips mid-connection the L4 proxy gets half the flow on a different path and resets. attaching short log snippet:

```
ASICSYS: ECMP_HASH_SEED_CHANGE port1->port5 reason=control-plane-swap
ASICSYS: hash_collisions++ from 3 -> 127 within 2m
LB: conn-track misses for 10.0.1.0/24 -> backend pool
```

Kaito: also saw RDMA fallback on a few workloads when this happened — once the path changed they downgraded to TCP and we surfaced MSS/PMTU warnings. That explains both increased latency and the reset churn.

Maria: mitigation plan tried so far:
- disabled ECMP group that showed seed instability on toprack-12 (canary)
- enabled sticky-hash on internal LB for the busy routes (sticky true on route-meta for warmup service)
- set net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 on gpu nodes to allow PMTU recovery
- scheduled mirror job to capture packets for a 30m window

Devon: quick results: after disabling ECMP group at 09:28 UTC errors on port1 tx_errors fell from 1023->12 by 09:40, gRPC resets dropped ~92%. Baseline jitter remains but dramatic reduction in resets. Still saw a tiny blip at 10:05 during a larger warmup run.

Chris: next steps:
- vendor opened a ticket for ASIC behaviour (possible firmware bug on ECMP seed roll)
- we'll keep sticky-hash in place for the warmup pool until vendor confirms a fix
- run controlled microburst tests with mirroring to validate path stability + RDMA behavior

Maria: operational action items assigned:
- @Kaito run mirroring capture and share pcap by EOD
- @Devon monitor for 24h and toggle warmup schedule if needed to reduce overlap with autoscaler events
- @Chris coordinate with vendor and provide ASIC counters

Devon: thanks all. schedule follow-up postmortem in #eng-infra tomorrow 11:00 PT. For now we have a working mitigation and rollback plan. :thumbsup:

SRE Rotation: acked — will watch pager for the next 12h and escalate if resets return above 3% baseline.
